subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a core/plugin-SDK capability-grant boundary for skills and plugin-owned tools, and should those grants be enforceable authorization or operator guardrails within the existing trusted-plugin model?
rationale: This choice determines the public taxonomy, default-deny and upgrade semantics, grant storage, enforcement coverage, audit guarantees, and whether the documented plugin trust boundary changes; repository inspection cannot safely choose those contracts.

options.title: Sponsor phased core contract
options.body: Approve manifest descriptors followed by persisted grants, pre-exposure filtering, execution-boundary checks, and SQLite auditing, while keeping contextual governance plugin-owned.

options.title: Limit scope to visibility
options.body: Make the inspect-only capability-manifest RFC canonical and defer grants and runtime enforcement until the trust and compatibility model is separately approved.

options.title: Retain current trust model
options.body: Keep name-based policy, sandboxing, approvals, and blocking hooks as the supported boundary and document governance plugins as optional defense in depth.

recommendation.title: Sponsor phased core contract
recommendation.body: Approve manifest descriptors followed by persisted grants, pre-exposure filtering, execution-boundary checks, and SQLite auditing, while keeping contextual governance plugin-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion and recent history place this person closest to the product vision, plugin manifest, gateway tool surfaces, and prior decision to retain this capability-grant question.
